h.strategy: After listing and negating default assumptions, keep only the negations that a general mechanism supports. Candidate mechanisms: parent quality (strong parents leave little room to improve and have more to lose), redundancy (duplicate or similar options dilute each other's contribution), and bottlenecks (an option matters little when it is not on the path to the output, however strong it is). Prefer predictions in which a usually helpful edit becomes neutral or harmful in a common context, or a usually harmful edit becomes harmless. Avoid conditions that only a few parents satisfy. Spread hypotheses across different edited fields and condition fields. Give at least four 'lower' predictions where the intuitive guess would be 'higher'.

hyps.why: With edge 0 removed, node 1 receives no input, so a conv on edge 4 carries nothing (bottleneck).
Node 2 is a dead end when edge 5 is none, so upgrading edge 1 cannot reach the output.
Edge 2 feeds only node 2, which is cut from the output when edge 5 is none, so the upgrade is wasted.
Replacing an existing conv gains much less than replacing a weak op, because the parent is already strong.
A second parallel skip into the output node duplicates the first and dilutes its contribution (redundancy).
With edge 4 removed, node 1 reaches the output only via edge 2 and node 2, so a stronger edge 0 is worth less.
Adding a direct input-to-output path where none existed gives a large gain, unlike replacing an existing conv.
Removing edge 0 hurts less when edge 4 is already none, since node 1's contribution to the output is already reduced.
Dropping edge 5 is less harmful when a direct skip into the output node keeps gradient flow and a fallback path.
A conv3x3 on edge 3 adds less when edge 5 already provides strong conv capacity into the same output node (redundancy).
